topic: Karnataka HC: wife's remarriage is a material change that can reduce permanent alimony, but does not by itself end it - Section 25 HMA (B v. Smt. A, MFA No. 1557 of 2023 (FC), 2026 LiveLaw (Kar) 421)

slides.title: Remarried after divorce? Your **alimony** can change
slides.subtitle: Remarriage is a big change in circumstances, but it does **not automatically** wipe out the right to alimony.
slides.cite: **B v. Smt. A**, MFA No. 1557 of 2023 (FC), 2026 LiveLaw (Kar) 421 · Justices D K Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan

slides.label: The case
slides.title: Divorce and **Rs 25 lakh** alimony
bullets: The couple married in **2021**. The wife alleged cruelty, and the Mysuru Family Court granted a **divorce**.
It awarded her **Rs 25 lakh** as permanent alimony. The husband earned Rs 25 lakh a year; the wife, Rs 7 lakh.
The husband appealed only against the **amount**, not the divorce.

slides.label: A new fact
slides.title: She **remarried** during the appeal
bullets: While the appeal was pending, the wife's own lawyer filed her marriage certificate: she had **remarried** in April 2024.
The husband argued this should **lower** the alimony. He also pointed to his dependent parents.

slides.label: What the court held
slides.title: Alimony is support, not a **prize**
bullets: **Section 25** of the Hindu Marriage Act lets a court change or cancel alimony when circumstances change. Section 25(3) covers **remarriage**.
Alimony is meant for **reasonable support**. It is not a windfall that ignores later events.
Remarriage is a **material change**, but not an automatic end. The award was cut to **Rs 10 lakh**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Proof decides the **amount**
bullets: There is **no fixed formula**. Courts weigh both sides' income, property, needs, status and later events.
The husband's other points failed because **no affidavit of assets and liabilities** was filed.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Does alimony stop if a divorced wife remarries? The answer is not a simple yes or no 💍⚖️

A couple married in 2021. The Family Court in Mysuru granted the wife a divorce and Rs 25 lakh as permanent alimony. The husband appealed only against the amount. While the appeal was pending, the wife remarried in April 2024.

The Karnataka High Court said Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act allows a court to change or cancel alimony when circumstances change, and Section 25(3) specifically covers remarriage. Alimony is meant for reasonable support, not a windfall. Remarriage is a material change that must be considered, but it does not by itself end the right. The alimony was reduced to Rs 10 lakh, and the divorce stayed as it was.

Tip: there is no fixed formula for alimony. The husband's other arguments failed because no affidavit of assets and liabilities was filed. Proper disclosure matters.

Case: B v. Smt. A, MFA No. 1557 of 2023 (FC), 2026 LiveLaw (Kar) 421
Bench: Justices D K Singh and H Shanthi Bhushan, Karnataka High Court
